column1: # JACOB LEIBHOLZ, 26 FEBRUARY 1943 — THE LINE ON THE LIST, AND HE WAS NOT TAKEN FROM HOME.
# Arolsen Archives, two documents read 20 September 2026 with David's consent declaration ticked.
# This archive has had Jacob's deportation date since the Bundesarchiv Gedenkbuch was checked on day
# two. What it has never had is the paperwork — and the paperwork moves him to a different street.
field
column2: value

column1: *** THE TRANSPORT LIST ITSELF ***
column2: DocID 127212355, in "Wave 44 — 30th OSTTRANSPORT TO CC AUSCHWITZ, 26 FEBRUARY 1943", reference 15510037, 59 documents. The scope note: a letter from the Stapoleitstelle Berlin to the Chief Finance President about confiscating the deportees' property, and a transport list of 1,100 names. Jacob is on page 153.

column1: his line, column by column
column2: Lfd. Nr. *** 1039 *** · Name LEIBHOLZ · Vorname JAKOB ISRAEL · geb. am 8.8.84 · Ort SCHUBIN · Beruf *** OHNE *** · verh. JA · Alter 58 · arbeitsfähig JA · Wohnung *** TREUCHTLINGERSTR. 4 *** · Kennkarten-Nr. A492552 (the third digit is not crisp) · Kennzeichen-Nr. 31822 · and a pencilled 1183 in the remarks.

column1: *** AND THE ADDRESS IS NOT THE FAMILY'S FLAT ***
column2: the 1939 census has JACOB, AUGUSTE AND SIEGFRIED TOGETHER AT MERANER STRASSE 2, SCHÖNEBERG. In February 1943 he is at TREUCHTLINGER STRASSE 4 — a different street in the same quarter, the Bayerisches Viertel. He had been moved out of his own home before the end, and the list records the new address, not the old one.

column1: the second document says the same and adds one word
column2: DocID 11243224, an AJDC/ITS index card in 1.2.1.2, reference 01020102 047 — the same card series as Oskar's, four numbers away from it. "Name LEIBHOLZ · First Names JACOB · Date of Birth 8.8.84 · PLACE OF BIRTH SCHUBIN/POSEN · LAST KNOWN ADDRESS BLN.-SCHÖNEBERG, TREUCHTLINGERSTR. 4 *** b/SPIER *** · Information 44/26011 U — 30. Osttrsp. 26.2.43".

column1: *** "b/SPIER" — AND THE SAME PAGE OF THE LIST PROVES WHAT IT MEANS ***
column2: b/ is bei, "care of". He was lodging with a family called SPIER. THIS IS NOT A GUESS ABOUT THE CONVENTION: the twenty lines above his on page 153 include "49 b/Grindel", "b/Gottfeld" and "b/Neumann" — deportees living in other people's flats. By 1943 Berlin Jews had been concentrated into shared housing, and Jacob is recorded as one of them.

column1: what the archive is NOT saying
column2: IT DOES NOT SAY WHEN HE MOVED, OR WHETHER HE WAS MADE TO. The census of 17 May 1939 and the list of 26 February 1943 are three years and nine months apart and nothing read here fills the gap. The word Judenhaus is not on either document and is not used here.

column1: *** BERUF: OHNE ***
column2: Jacob traded as JAQUES. The 1938 Berliner Adressbuch has "Jaques (Kaufm, Schöneberg, MERANER STR 2)" and "Jaques Leibholz & Co (Konfektion, W8 Krausenstr 59.60)" — a merchant with a clothing firm on Krausenstraße. The transport list of 1943 gives his occupation as OHNE. NONE.

column1: and "arbeitsfähig: ja"
column2: fit for work, at fifty-eight. The column exists because the answer determined what happened on arrival. Recorded, and nothing is inferred from it here.

column1: the wave number
column2: 44/26011 on the card, and the list calls itself Wave 44. OSKAR'S CARD READS 49/30999 AND THE 4TH ALTERSTRANSPORT. The two brothers went on two different waves nineteen days apart — Jacob east to Auschwitz on 26 February, Oskar to Theresienstadt on 17 March — and the same office numbered them both.

column1: *** SAMUEL, RE-TESTED WITH THE CONSENT TICKED, IS STILL NOT THERE ***
column2: a search for "Leibholz Samuel" in the Arolsen person index returns NOTHING, exactly as it did on 17 September before the consent was given. The Gedenkbuch and Yad Vashem both have him — born Schubin 28 June 1877, died Auschwitz 10 April 1943 — and this archive does not. The absence is now tested twice and it is the archive's, not the search's.

column1: source
column2: Arolsen Archives, collections.arolsen-archives.org — DocIDs 127212355 and 11243224, images read 20 September 2026 with the consent declaration ticked by David.

column1: # ——— ADDED THE SAME DAY: THE 1939 CENSUS, SEARCHED BY ADDRESS, NAMES THE SPIERS ———
*** TREUCHTLINGER STRASSE 4 ON CENSUS NIGHT, 17 MAY 1939 ***
column2: SEVENTEEN PERSECUTED PEOPLE IN ONE BUILDING, from eleven family names: BRÜCK Hedwig 17.05.1892 · COHN Erna 29.11.1888 † 25.11.1941 · EISENBERG Trude née Haake 09.06.1879 · EISENBERGER Lisbeth 23.06.1888 · KAPHAN Heinz 05.06.1916 and Lucie 28.07.1888 · KOCHANOWSKA Franziska 30.09.1893 · LÖWENHEIM Paul 21.01.1873 and Marie Luise née Sachse 17.04.1894 · PODBIELSKI Rose 26.07.1900 · ROSENSTOCK Leo 08.01.1886 and Franziska née Flügelmann 14.08.1896 · SUNDHEIMER Max 19.09.1877 and Gertrude née David 14.08.1881 — and the SPIERS.

column1: *** AND THE SPIERS ARE NAMED ***
column2: SPIER, MAX, born 12.04.1864, DIED 26 MARCH 1941 · SPIER, HANS, born 02.12.1894, died before 08.05.1945 · SPIER, ALICE née WOLLSTEIN, born 03.11.1899, died before 08.05.1945. The "b/Spier" on Jacob's AJDC card is a household with three names in it, and by the time he was lodging with them the eldest was already dead.

column1: what that makes the building
column2: A HOUSE ALREADY FULL OF CONCENTRATED JEWISH HOUSEHOLDS IN MAY 1939, three and a half years before Jacob was moved into it. Eleven surnames at one address is not an ordinary Berlin apartment block. JACOB IS NOT IN THE 1939 LIST FOR IT, because on census night he was still at Meraner Straße 2 with his wife and son.

column1: # *** AND THE SAME SEARCH, RUN ON MERANER STRASSE 2, EXPLAINS THE SHEET NOBODY COULD EXPLAIN ***
MERANER STRASSE 2 ON CENSUS NIGHT
column2: FOURTEEN at the address: LEIBHOLZ Jacob, Auguste née Luwinski and Siegfried · PEYSER Selma Slowe née Salinger 07.09.1873 † 24.12.1943 · *** PUFF, ANNA, born 01.06.1895 *** · SALINGER Wolff 17.04.1878 † 13.07.1939 and Elise née Bleistein 06.06.1889 † 16.02.1940 · SCHADE Friedrich 30.09.1906, Klara née Fuchs 10.05.1902 and Heinz 30.07.1933 · SCHLESINGER Fanny née Grünthal 25.09.1866 † 24.08.1942 and Edith 11.07.1898 · WEIL Ida née Frank 26.08.1892.

column1: *** ANNA PUFF IS ON THE SECOND IMAGE OF THE LEIBHOLZ REGISTRATION CARD ***
column2: DocID 11214358 indexes ELEVEN people across its two images, and the seven this archive could not place were SCHMIDT Else · PUFF Anna 01.06.1895 · HEINICKE Anna · HERZOG Else · BIERE Henriette · KOCH Erika · NICKSCH Klara. ANNA PUFF, BORN 1 JUNE 1895, IS AT MERANER STRASSE 2 IN THE 1939 CENSUS, TO THE DAY.

column1: so the second sheet has a name now
column2: IT IS THE HOUSE LIST FOR MERANER STRASSE 2 — the other households in the Leibholz family's own building. That is exactly what the stamp on the FIRST image says it should be: "LT. HAUSLISTE 1945 N. ERFASST", according to the house list of 1945, not recorded. The card and the list belong together and were filmed together.

column1: *** THE READING WAS THEN TESTED AGAINST THE 1939 DIRECTORY, AND IT SURVIVES ***
column2: the Teil IV entry for Meraner Straße 2 (image 5902, printed page 1598) lists the householders: Salomonski as owner, then Binder, Briliant, Dübe, Dunje, Gadischle & Kaulmann, Hesler, Helm, Kamnitzer, v. Koch, *** LEIBHOLZ, J., KFM. ***, Neumann, Pehser, Putzar-Ehrenberg, Schade twice, Wesse. NONE OF THE SHEET'S OTHER SIX NAMES IS AMONG THEM. That is not fatal for two ordinary reasons: the directory lists HOUSEHOLDERS ONLY — Anna Puff is in the census at that address and not in the directory either — and the stamp says HAUSLISTE 1945, a list made six years and a war later in a city where the bombed-out were rehoused constantly. THE READING NOW HAS A TEST BEHIND IT INSTEAD OF ONE MATCH, AND IT IS STILL A READING.

column1: the bound on that reading, and it is one match out of seven
column2: ONLY ANNA PUFF MATCHES. Schmidt, Heinicke, Herzog, Biere, Koch and Nicksch are not in the census database for that address — but THAT DATABASE HOLDS PERSECUTED PEOPLE, not every Berliner, so non-Jewish neighbours would not be in it whatever house they lived in. ONE EXACT MATCH PLUS THE STAMP IS A STRONG READING AND IT IS NOT A PROOF. Recorded as the best account of the sheet, replacing "a sheet of other households" and not claiming more.

column1: and it puts Kurt on the sheet for a reason
column2: if image 002 is the house list for Meraner Straße 2, then LUWINSKI, KURT, 11.5.12 is written on it as a member of the Leibholz household — an absent son recorded against his parents' flat. That is a reading and not a record, and it is the third different account this archive has given of why his name is on that DocID. IT IS OFFERED AS THE BEST ONE AND FLAGGED AS THE THIRD.
